message.content:
The repository at /home/user/adss-2026-09-07, branch claude/adss-slice-04-revenue-per-order-month (slice 4 just
landed and is green). Read whatever you need; do NOT modify any file.

The system is an "Analytical Data Storage System": DAS (das/, contracts over recorded OData
fixtures, hive-partitioned parquet, das__raw + das__staged) -> DAB (dab/model.yaml, mappings,
the daana-cli modelling engine, schema dab) -> DAR (generated Unified Star Schema, dar__uss)
-> destinations/ (one marimo page, a section per question). Analytical usage reads only
dar__uss; dar reads only dab; dab reads only das.

Slice 5's question, from docs/questions/README.md:
  "What revenue did we take per product category and quarter?" -- asked by a category manager.
  What it widens: two more contracts and a TWO-HOP relationship chain, line -> product ->
  category.

Everything already decided is in docs/adr/0000..0013, docs/conventions.md, docs/blueprint.md
and docs/deviations.md. Slice 4 added: ORDER_LINE at a finer grain, an inherited event date
(ADR 0009), a composed composite key (ADR 0010), the fan-out proof and the rule that an answer
query may aggregate only _measure__ columns (ADR 0012), and one clock per ingest (ADR 0013).

The source is the Northwind OData demo service at
https://demodata.grapecity.com/northwind/odata/v1 (recorded under das/fixtures/). Products and
Categories are entity sets there.


YOUR JOB: draft the OPTIONS AND CONSEQUENCES for the single decision slice 5 forces, well
enough that a MADR can be written from it.

The decision is about the TWO-HOP CHAIN: an order line points at a product, and a product
points at a category, and the question groups revenue by the category. Nothing in this system
has ever walked two edges.

Work out, from the code rather than from first principles:
- What the generator does today with a walk of more than one edge. Read src/adss/uss.py --
  entity_ids, entity_keys, _inherit_cte, _stage_cte, _branch -- and say exactly what happens
  if ORDER_LINE reaches PRODUCT and PRODUCT reaches CATEGORY. Does the bridge get a
  category_key at all? Does the peripheral for CATEGORY exist? Is the walk transitive or one
  hop deep? Quote the code.
- What the modelling engine gives us. The dab and dar skills under .claude/skills/ record what
  daana-cli actually does on DuckDB, including that focal and identifier tables are never
  populated and that relationship keys come from v_<src>_<name>_<tgt>. Say what a second hop
  would need from the engine.
- The candidate options. At least: (a) make the bridge's walk transitive, so a stage carries
  the key of everything it reaches at any depth; (b) keep one hop and denormalise the category
  onto the product peripheral; (c) keep one hop and let the question join peripheral to
  peripheral in dar__uss; (d) anything else the code suggests. For each: what it costs, what
  it makes impossible later, and which existing ADR or convention it sits against.
- Which of the blog's own principles bear on it (docs/blueprint.md is the technology-free
  statement of them).

Quote file and line for every claim about what the code does. Where you are guessing, say so.
Do not recommend one option; lay them out.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adss: The whole system — how the three layers fit, how a slice is built and accepted, and what to read before changing anything. Use when starting work on this repository, adding a slice or a business question, deciding which layer a change belongs in, or when a change seems to need two layers at once.
- dab: Work on the DAB layer — dab/model.yaml, the mappings, and the modelling engine. Use when adding an entity, attribute or relationship, editing anything under dab/, running install/deploy/execute, or debugging engine errors, history that looks wrong, or rows that multiply.
- dar: Work on the DAR layer — the generated Unified Star Schema, dab/uss.yaml, and the SQL under dar/uss. Use when adding an event or a measure, changing the bridge's column contract, debugging a total that is wrong or multiplied, or when generated SQL and the model have drifted.
- das: Work on the DAS layer — data contracts, the dlt landing zone, and the raw and staged views. Use when adding or changing a source, editing das/contracts/*.yaml, touching src/adss/{contract,das,landing,source}.py, re-recording fixtures, or debugging why a column is missing, mistyped, or duplicated in das__staged.
- destination: Work on the marimo destination — the page that presents a question and its answer, and the screenshots a slice is accepted on. Use when adding a page for a new question, changing a chart, or when a screenshot is blank, truncated or fails to render.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers a dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- grill-to-build: Interview to exhaustion, then a plan I confirm, then a  workflow per slice. Use for any build run from a brief.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

119	            aggregate = Aggregate(str(raw["aggregate"]))
120	            if "definition" not in raw:
121	                raise UssError(f"{path}: measure {raw['id']} has no definition.")
122	            attribute_id = str(raw["attribute"]).strip() if raw.get("attribute") else None
123	            if aggregate is Aggregate.SUM and not attribute_id:
124	                raise UssError(
125	                    f"{path}: measure {raw['id']} declares aggregate: sum and names nothing "
126	                    f"to sum. A blank attribute would emit a column named after nothing."
127	                )
128	            measures.append(
129	                Measure(
130	                    id=_named(str(raw["id"])),
131	                    definition=str(raw["definition"]),
132	                    aggregate=aggregate,
133	                    attribute_id=attribute_id,
134	                )
135	            )
136	        events.append(
137	            Event(
138	                id=event_id,
139	                entity_id=str(declared["entity"]),
140	                definition=str(declared["definition"]),
141	                kind=EventKind(str(declared["kind"])),
142	                date_attribute_id=str(declared["date_attribute"]),
143	                measures=tuple(measures),
144	            )
145	        )
146	    uss = Uss(path=path, events=tuple(events))
147	    resolved = model or _model_beside(path)
148	    _refuse_edges_that_would_collide(resolved)
149	    _refuse_measures_that_would_share_a_name(uss)
150	    _refuse_measures_of_things_that_are_not_numbers(uss, resolved)
151	    return uss
152	
153	
154	def _model_beside(path: Path) -> Model:
155	    from adss.model import read_model
156	
157	    return read_model(path.parent / "model.yaml")
158	
159	
160	def _refuse_edges_that_would_collide(model: Model) -> None:
161	    """Two edges into one key column is a silent loss, so it is refused rather than emitted.
162	
163	    A stage carries one column per entity it inherits from, named for that entity. Two edges
164	    from one entity to the same target -- or an edge to the entity itself -- would emit two
165	    columns of the same name, and DuckDB resolves that ambiguity instead of raising, so one of
166	    the two inherited keys vanishes with nothing to say which. Distinguishing them means naming
167	    the column after the edge rather than the target, which changes a published contract, so it
168	    is a decision for the slice that first needs two such edges rather than a shape to guess at
169	    now. ADR 0006.
170	    """
171	    for entity in model.entities:
172	        edges = model.edges_from(entity.id)
173	        for edge in edges:
174	            if edge.target_entity_id == entity.id:
175	                raise UssError(
176	                    f"{edge.id} points at the entity it runs from, so the stage would carry "
177	                    f"{entity.key_column} twice under one name and lose one of them silently."
178	                )
179	        targets = [edge.target_entity_id for edge in edges]
180	        for target in targets:
181	            if targets.count(target) > 1:
182	                colliding = [edge.id for edge in edges if edge.target_entity_id == target]
183	                raise UssError(
184	                    f"{' and '.join(colliding)} both inherit into "
185	                    f"{model.entity(target).key_column}, and a stage carrying that column "
186	                    f"twice loses one of them with no error. Naming the column after the edge "
187	                    f"rather than the target would fix it and would change the bridge's "
188	                    f"published contract, so it is a decision rather than a patch."
189	                )
190	
191	
192	def _refuse_measures_that_would_share_a_name(uss: Uss) -> None:
193	    """Two events on one entity may not declare the same measure id. ADR 0008.
194	
195	    A measure is owned by an event and named for an entity. While an entity has one event those
196	    are the same thing; with two they are not, and the same id on both emits one column twice
197	    AND silently replaces one definition with the other in the glossary.
198	
199	    The column half would fail the build loudly -- DuckDB renames the second column rather than
200	    raising, so the built table stops matching the published contract. The glossary half is
201	    caught by nothing: no check inspects the definitions, and they are what a question's
202	    references resolve against and what the page renders. A reader would be shown a plausible
203	    sentence about the wrong number, and everything would pass.
204	    """
205	    seen: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
206	    for event in uss.events:
207	        for measure in event.measures:
208	            key = (event.entity_id, measure.id)
209	            if key in seen:
210	                raise UssError(
211	                    f"{event.entity_id} declares {measure.id} on both {seen[key]} and "
212	                    f"{event.id}. A measure is named for its entity and owned by its event, so "
213	                    f"the two would share one column -- and {event.id}'s definition would "
214	                    f"replace {seen[key]}'s in the glossary, which nothing checks and the page "
215	                    f"renders. Give them separate ids, or one definition covering both."
216	                )
217	            seen[key] = event.id
218	
219	
220	def _refuse_measures_of_things_that_are_not_numbers(uss: Uss, model: Model) -> None:
221	    for event in uss.events:
222	        if event.kind is not EventKind.TRANSACTION:
223	            raise UssError(
224	                f"{event.id} is declared {event.kind}, and the generator only builds "
225	                f"transaction stages. It would emit a transaction stage anyway and mark "
226	                f"every row current, which is worse than refusing: nothing downstream could "
227	                f"tell. A snapshot stage arrives in the slice that first needs one."
228	            )
229	        entity = model.entity(event.entity_id)
230	        inherited, attribute_id = event.dated_by
231	        if inherited is not None:
232	            reachable = {edge.target_entity_id for edge in model.edges_from(entity.id)}
233	            if inherited not in reachable:
234	                raise UssError(
235	                    f"{event.id} is dated by {event.date_attribute_id}, and no edge reaches "
236	                    f"{inherited} from {entity.id}. {entity.id} reaches "
237	                    f"{sorted(reachable) or 'nothing'}. A date inherits along a declared edge "
238	                    f"or it does not inherit at all."
239	                )
240	        # A separate name: the measures below belong to the EVENT's entity, not to the one the
241	        # date is inherited from, and reusing `entity` here silently checked them against it.
242	        dater = model.entity(inherited) if inherited is not None else entity
243	        if not dater.attribute(attribute_id).is_date:
244	            raise UssError(f"{event.id} is dated by {attribute_id}, which is not a date.")
245	        for measure in event.measures:
246	            if measure.attribute_id is None:
247	                continue
248	            # By name, not by KeyError. A measure of an attribute the event's entity does not
249	            # have is exactly what a reader that checked measures against the inherited entity
250	            # would accept, so the refusal says whose attribute it is rather than dying.
251	            if measure.attribute_id not in {a.id for a in entity.attributes}:
252	                elsewhere = (
253	                    f" {dater.id} has it and {entity.id} does not"
254	                    if dater is not entity
255	                    and measure.attribute_id in {a.id for a in dater.attributes}
256	                    else ""
257	                )
258	                raise UssError(
259	                    f"{event.id}.{measure.id} sums {measure.attribute_id}, which {entity.id} "
260	                    f"does not have. A measure belongs to the entity of its own event, never "
261	                    f"to one the event inherits a date from.{elsewhere}"
262	                )
263	            if not entity.attribute(measure.attribute_id).is_number:
264	                raise UssError(
265	                    f"{event.id}.{measure.id} sums {measure.attribute_id}, which is not a "
266	                    f"number. Summing what is not a number produces a number nobody can read."
267	                )
268	
269	
270	def _version_cte(model: Model, event: Event) -> str:
271	    """The version of each entity this event is measured on: the latest in which it is dated."""
272	    entity = model.entity(event.entity_id)
273	    inherited, attribute_id = event.dated_by
274	    date = crossing(attribute_id)
275	    held = "revision"
276	    lines = [
277	        f"    {held}.{crossing(entity.source_key)} AS {entity.key_column}",
278	        f"    {held}.eff_tmstp AS _observed_at",
279	    ]
280	    # An inherited date is resolved with the key, in the CTE that walks the edge, so both are
281	    # true as of one instant. ADR 0009.
282	    if inherited is None:
283	        lines.append(f"    cast({held}.{date} AS DATE) AS _event_date")
284	    for measure in event.measures:
285	        column = f"_measure__{entity.object_name}__{measure.id.lower()}"
286	        if measure.aggregate is Aggregate.COUNT:
287	            value = f"cast(1 AS {COUNT_TYPE})"
288	        else:
289	            attribute = crossing(str(measure.attribute_id))
290	            value = f"cast({held}.{attribute} AS {SUM_TYPE})"
291	        lines.append(f"    {value} AS {column}")
292	    selected = ",\n".join(lines)
293	    # An inherited date is filtered where it is resolved, not here: this entity has no such
294	    # column to filter on.
295	    dated = "" if inherited else f"WHERE {held}.{date} IS NOT NULL\n"
296	    return (
297	        f"{event.name}__version AS (\n"
298	        f"SELECT\n{selected}\n"
299	        f'FROM dab."view_{entity.id}_hist" AS {held}\n'
300	        f"{dated}"
301	        f"QUALIFY row_number() OVER (\n"
302	        f"    PARTITION BY {held}.{crossing(entity.source_key)}\n"
303	        f"    ORDER BY {held}.eff_tmstp DESC\n"
304	        f") = 1\n"
305	        f")"
306	    )
307	
308	
309	def _inherit_cte(model: Model, event: Event, edge: Relationship) -> str:
310	    """One inherited key: the pair in force when the inheriting row was observed. ADR 0006.
311	
312	    Resolved per inheriting ROW rather than per key -- the partition carries the observation
313	    time -- because that is the whole reason ADR 0006 chose the observation time over "now".
314	    A stage that kept more than the latest version of an entity would otherwise hand every one
315	    of those versions the same parent, which is "as of now" wearing the other rule's clothes.
316	
317	    Read from `v_<SRC>_<NAME>_<TGT>`, which is the raw pairs plus the relationship's name, and
318	    ranked here rather than by the engine. The engine's own ranked view answers a different
319	    question -- who the parent is *now* -- and answers it with `rank()`, which returns two rows
320	    for a child whose source named two parents at one instant. Two rows here would double that
321	    child's measures, so the ranking is `row_number()` and the tie is refused by a data check.
322	    """
323	    source = model.entity(edge.source_entity_id)
324	    target = model.entity(edge.target_entity_id)
325	    held = edge.id.lower()
326	    # If the event is dated by this target's attribute, the date is resolved here, off the same
327	    # parent the key came from, so both are true as of one instant. ADR 0009.
328	    inherited, attribute_id = event.dated_by
329	    dates = inherited == target.id
330	    carried = f",\n    cast(dated.{crossing(attribute_id)} AS DATE) AS _event_date" if dates else ""
331	    # The candidate versions are the DATED ones. Without that clause the latest version wins
332	    # even when it is the one that blanked the date -- an ordinary shape in a full change log --
333	    # and the child's date is null, so ADR 0009's own rule removes its row. A whole grain then
334	    # leaves the bridge while the parent's own event stays dated, and nothing says so.
335	    joined = (
336	        f'\nLEFT JOIN dab."view_{target.id}_hist" AS dated\n'
337	        f"    ON dated.{crossing(target.source_key)} = pair.{crossing(target.source_key)}\n"
338	        f"    AND dated.{crossing(attribute_id)} IS NOT NULL\n"
339	        f"    AND dated.eff_tmstp <= revision._observed_at"
340	        if dates
341	        else ""
342	    )
343	    return (
344	        f"{event.name}__{held} AS (\n"
345	        f"SELECT\n"
346	        f"    revision.{source.key_column} AS {source.key_column},\n"
347	        f"    revision._observed_at AS _observed_at,\n"
348	        f"    pair.{crossing(target.source_key)} AS {target.key_column}"
349	        f"{carried}\n"
350	        f"FROM {event.name}__version AS revision\n"
351	        f'LEFT JOIN dab."v_{edge.id}" AS pair\n'
352	        f"    ON pair.{crossing(source.source_key)} = revision.{source.key_column}\n"
353	        f"    AND pair.rel_name = '{edge.id}'\n"
354	        f"    AND pair.row_st = 'Y'\n"
355	        f"    AND pair.eff_tmstp <= revision._observed_at"
356	        f"{joined}\n"
357	        f"QUALIFY row_number() OVER (\n"
358	        f"    PARTITION BY revision.{source.key_column}, revision._observed_at\n"
359	        f"    ORDER BY\n"
360	        f"        pair.eff_tmstp DESC,\n"
361	        f"        pair.ver_tmstp DESC,\n"
362	        f"        pair.{crossing(target.source_key)}"
363	        + (",\n        dated.eff_tmstp DESC" if dates else "")
364	        + "\n) = 1\n"
365	        ")"
366	    )
367	
368	
369	def _stage_cte(model: Model, event: Event) -> str:
370	    """One stage: the entity's version, with the key of everything it inherits from."""
371	    entity = model.entity(event.entity_id)
372	    edges = model.edges_from(entity.id)
373	    inherited, _ = event.dated_by
374	    dater = "revision"
375	    if inherited is not None:
376	        dater = next(edge.id.lower() for edge in edges if edge.target_entity_id == inherited)
377	    lines = [
378	        f"    revision.{entity.key_column} AS {entity.key_column}",
379	        "    revision._observed_at AS _observed_at",
380	        f"    {dater}._event_date AS _event_date",
381	    ]
382	    lines += [
383	        f"    {edge.id.lower()}.{model.entity(edge.target_entity_id).key_column} "
384	        f"AS {model.entity(edge.target_entity_id).key_column}"
385	        for edge in edges
386	    ]
387	    lines += [
388	        f"    revision._measure__{entity.object_name}__{measure.id.lower()} "
389	        f"AS _measure__{entity.object_name}__{measure.id.lower()}"
390	        for measure in event.measures
391	    ]
392	    # One row per inheriting row in each of these, so none of the joins can fan out. LEFT
393	    # anyway: the row that inherits nothing is kept by the join inside the CTE, and an inner
394	    # join here would undo that one level up.
395	    joins = "".join(
396	        f"\nLEFT JOIN {event.name}__{edge.id.lower()} AS {edge.id.lower()}\n"
397	        f"    ON {edge.id.lower()}.{entity.key_column} = revision.{entity.key_column}\n"
398	        f"    AND {edge.id.lower()}._observed_at = revision._observed_at"
399	        for edge in edges
400	    )
401	    selected = ",\n".join(lines)
402	    # An event's own date is filtered in the version CTE; an inherited one is not there to
403	    # filter, so it is filtered where it was resolved. Same rule, one step along the walk: a
404	    # row whose date does not resolve is absent rather than dated null -- and the calendar's
405	    # inner join would otherwise drop it silently, which looks like the rule working. ADR 0009.
406	    absent = "" if inherited is None else f"\nWHERE {dater}._event_date IS NOT NULL"
407	    return (
408	        f"{event.name} AS (\nSELECT\n{selected}\n"
409	        f"FROM {event.name}__version AS revision{joins}{absent}\n)"
410	    )
411	
412	
413	def _branch(model: Model, uss: Uss, event: Event, keys: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
414	    """One branch of the union: this stage's own columns, and a typed NULL for the rest."""
415	    entity = model.entity(event.entity_id)
416	    carried = {entity.key_column} | {
417	        model.entity(edge.target_entity_id).key_column for edge in model.edges_from(entity.id)
418	    }
419	    lines = [
420	        f"    '{entity.object_name}' AS _stage",
421	        f"    '{event.name}' AS _event",
422	        f"    {event.name}._event_date AS _event_date",
423	        "    TRUE AS _is_current",
424	        f"    {event.name}._observed_at AS _observed_at",
425	    ]
426	    for key in keys:
427	        value = f"{event.name}.{key}" if key in carried else "cast(NULL AS VARCHAR)"
428	        lines.append(f"    {value} AS {key}")
429	    owned = {column for candidate, _, column in uss.measure_columns() if candidate is event}
430	    for _, measure, column in uss.measure_columns():
431	        value = f"{event.name}.{column}" if column in owned else f"cast(NULL AS {measure.sql_type})"
432	        lines.append(f"    {value} AS {column}")
433	    return "SELECT\n" + ",\n".join(lines) + f"\nFROM {event.name} AS {event.name}"
434	
435	
436	def entity_ids(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> tuple[str, ...]:
437	    """Every entity the bridge names, in MODEL order: the ones with events, and the ones they
438	    inherit from. An entity reached only by inheritance still needs a peripheral, or the bridge
439	    carries a key that joins to nothing.
440	    """
441	    touched = {event.entity_id for event in uss.events}
442	    touched |= {
443	        edge.target_entity_id for event in uss.events for edge in model.edges_from(event.entity_id)
444	    }
445	    return tuple(entity.id for entity in model.entities if entity.id in touched)
446	
447	
448	def entity_keys(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> tuple[str, ...]:
449	    """One key column per entity the bridge names, in MODEL order.
450	
451	    Model order, not event order: reordering two events in the sidecar is not a model change,
452	    and it must not rearrange a contract that consumers are written against. The check cannot
453	    catch that on its own, because it derives what it expects from this same function.
454	    """
455	    return tuple(model.entity(entity_id).key_column for entity_id in entity_ids(model, uss))
456	
457	
458	def bridge_columns(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> tuple[str, ...]:
459	    """The published column contract, in order.
460	
461	    Grouped: the structural columns, then one key per entity in model order, then one column
462	    per measure in declaration order.
463	
464	    That grouping means the contract does NOT only ever grow at the end, and saying otherwise
465	    would be the more comfortable lie. A new entity appends a key, and because keys precede
466	    measures, every measure column moves right. An entity inserted in the middle of the model
467	    moves the keys after it as well. So the model file's own order is part of this contract,
468	    and nothing here can catch a rearrangement: the check that compares the built bridge to
469	    this contract derives what it expects from this same function, so both sides move together
470	    and it passes either way.
471	
472	    What makes that tolerable rather than a defect is that nothing reads this table by
473	    position. Conventions section 3 forbids `SELECT *`, the questions name their columns and
474	    so does the destination. A consumer that did read positionally would be reading a contract
475	    this docstring does not offer it. New entities still go at the end, because moving a key
476	    column is a bigger change than moving a measure. Blueprint B7.
477	    """
478	    keys = entity_keys(model, uss)
479	    structural = ("_stage", "_event", "_event_date", "_is_current", "_observed_at")
480	    return structural + keys + tuple(column for _, _, column in uss.measure_columns())
481	
482	
483	def bridge_sql(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> str:
484	    """One row per measurement event, over every stage the declarations name."""
485	    keys = entity_keys(model, uss)
486	    ctes = ",\n\n".join(
487	        cte
488	        for event in uss.events
489	        for cte in (
490	            _version_cte(model, event),
491	            *(_inherit_cte(model, event, edge) for edge in model.edges_from(event.entity_id)),
492	            _stage_cte(model, event),
493	        )
494	    )
495	    branches = "\n\nUNION ALL\n\n".join(_branch(model, uss, event, keys) for event in uss.events)
496	    return f"{_GENERATED}\nCREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {BRIDGE.sql} AS\nWITH {ctes}\n\n{branches};\n"
497	
498	
499	def peripheral_sql(model: Model, entity_id: str) -> str:
500	    """One row per entity instance, current state, key first and attributes as declared."""
501	    entity: Entity = model.entity(entity_id)
502	    lines = [
503	        f"    e.{crossing(entity.source_key)} AS {entity.key_column}",
504	        "    e.eff_tmstp AS _observed_at",
505	    ]
506	    lines += [f"    e.{crossing(a.id)} AS {a.column}" for a in entity.attributes]
507	    selected = ",\n".join(lines)
508	    relation = Relation(Schema.DAR_USS, entity.object_name)
509	    return (
510	        f"{_GENERATED}\n"
511	        f"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {relation.sql} AS\n"
512	        f"SELECT\n{selected}\n"
513	        f'FROM dab."view_{entity.id}_hist" AS e\n'
514	        f"QUALIFY row_number() OVER (\n"
515	        f"    PARTITION BY e.{crossing(entity.source_key)}\n"
516	        f"    ORDER BY e.eff_tmstp DESC\n"
517	        f") = 1;\n"
518	    )
519	
520	
521	def calendar_sql() -> str:
522	    """Dense and daily across everything the bridge holds. Civil arithmetic only.
523	
524	    A calendar containing only the days something happened is not a calendar: a month with
525	    no events must still appear in a time series. Fiscal periods and holidays are business
526	    meaning and would need a definition, so they belong in the model, not in a generator.
527	    """
528	    return (
529	        f"{_GENERATED}\n"
530	        f"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {CALENDAR.sql} AS\n"
531	        f"WITH bounds AS (\n"
532	        f"SELECT\n"
533	        f"    min(b._event_date) AS first_date,\n"
534	        f"    max(b._event_date) AS last_date\n"
535	        f"FROM {BRIDGE.sql} AS b\n"
536	        f"),\n\n"
537	        f"every_day AS (\n"
538	        f"SELECT\n"
539	        f"    cast(d.day AS DATE) AS date_key\n"
540	        f"FROM bounds AS bo\n"
541	        f"CROSS JOIN range(\n"
542	        f"    bo.first_date, bo.last_date + INTERVAL 1 DAY, INTERVAL 1 DAY\n"
543	        f") AS d (day)\n"
544	        f")\n\n"
545	        f"SELECT\n"
546	        f"    d.date_key AS date_key,\n"
547	        f"    cast(year(d.date_key) AS INTEGER) AS year_number,\n"
548	        f"    cast(quarter(d.date_key) AS INTEGER) AS quarter_of_year,\n"
549	        f"    cast(month(d.date_key) AS INTEGER) AS month_of_year,\n"
550	        f"    cast(day(d.date_key) AS INTEGER) AS day_of_month,\n"
551	        f"    cast(date_trunc('year', d.date_key) AS DATE) AS year_start,\n"
552	        f"    cast(date_trunc('quarter', d.date_key) AS DATE) AS quarter_start,\n"
553	        f"    cast(date_trunc('month', d.date_key) AS DATE) AS month_start,\n"
554	        f"    strftime(d.date_key, '%Y') || '-Q' || cast(quarter(d.date_key) AS VARCHAR) "
555	        f"AS quarter_label,\n"
556	        f"    strftime(d.date_key, '%Y-%m') AS month_label\n"
557	        f"FROM every_day AS d;\n"
558	    )
559	
560	
561	def definitions(model: Model, uss: Uss) -> dict[str, str]:
562	    """Every definition, by the token that refers to it. Copied verbatim, never composed.
563	
564	    A generator that composed a definition would be a third place the data is explained,
565	    and the worst kind: one nobody wrote and nobody reviews.
566	    """
567	    found = dict(model.definitions())
568	    for event in uss.events:
569	        found[f"{event.entity_id}.events.{event.id}"] = event.definition
570	        for measure in event.measures:
571	            found[f"{event.entity_id}.measures.{measure.id}"] = measure.definition
572	    return found

1	"""A structural reading of the business model. It carries meaning; it never reads it.
     2	
     3	The definitions in the model are the only explanation of the data there is. This module
     4	moves them around -- into a glossary, into a check that a question's references resolve --
     5	and never composes one, because a composed definition is a second explanation that nobody
     6	wrote and nobody reviews.
     7	"""
     8	
     9	from __future__ import annotations
    10	
    11	from dataclasses import dataclass
    12	from enum import StrEnum
    13	from pathlib import Path
    14	
    15	import yaml
    16	
    17	from adss.names import refuse_unsafe, unsafe
    18	
    19	
    20	class AttributeType(StrEnum):
    21	    """The modelling language's whole type vocabulary. Semantic, not physical."""
    22	
    23	    STRING = "STRING"
    24	    NUMBER = "NUMBER"
    25	    UNIT = "UNIT"
    26	    START_TIMESTAMP = "START_TIMESTAMP"
    27	    END_TIMESTAMP = "END_TIMESTAMP"
    28	
    29	
    30	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    31	class Attribute:
    32	    id: str
    33	    type: AttributeType
    34	    definition: str
    35	
    36	    @property
    37	    def column(self) -> str:
    38	        """How this attribute is spelled in the generated layer."""
    39	        return self.id.lower()
    40	
    41	    @property
    42	    def is_number(self) -> bool:
    43	        return self.type is AttributeType.NUMBER
    44	
    45	    @property
    46	    def is_date(self) -> bool:
    47	        return self.type in (AttributeType.START_TIMESTAMP, AttributeType.END_TIMESTAMP)
    48	
    49	
    50	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    51	class Entity:
    52	    id: str
    53	    definition: str
    54	    attributes: tuple[Attribute, ...]
    55	
    56	    @property
    57	    def object_name(self) -> str:
    58	        """The generated layer's name for this entity: snake_case, singular."""
    59	        return self.id.lower()
    60	
    61	    @property
    62	    def key_column(self) -> str:
    63	        return f"{self.object_name}_key"
    64	
    65	    @property
    66	    def source_key(self) -> str:
    67	        """What the modelling engine calls this entity's key, in its own casing."""
    68	        return f"{self.id}_key"
    69	
    70	    def attribute(self, attribute_id: str) -> Attribute:
    71	        for attribute in self.attributes:
    72	            if attribute.id == attribute_id:
    73	                return attribute
    74	        raise KeyError(f"{self.id} has no attribute {attribute_id!r}")
    75	
    76	
    77	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    78	class Relationship:
    79	    """A many-to-one edge, along which a key inherits and a measure does not.
    80	
    81	    That it is many-to-one is not stated here, because the modelling language has nowhere to
    82	    state it: `cardinality` is rejected and `type` is dropped on compile. It is inferred from
    83	    the mapping's shape and pinned by a data check. ADR 0006.
    84	    """
    85	
    86	    name: str
    87	    source_entity_id: str
    88	    target_entity_id: str
    89	    definition: str
    90	
    91	    @property
    92	    def id(self) -> str:
    93	        """`<SRC>_<NAME>_<TGT>`, which is how every object the engine builds is named."""
    94	        return f"{self.source_entity_id}_{self.name}_{self.target_entity_id}"
    95	
    96	
    97	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    98	class Model:
    99	    path: Path
   100	    entities: tuple[Entity, ...]
   101	    relationships: tuple[Relationship, ...] = ()
   102	
   103	    def entity(self, entity_id: str) -> Entity:
   104	        for entity in self.entities:
   105	            if entity.id == entity_id:
   106	                return entity
   107	        raise KeyError(f"{self.path} has no entity {entity_id!r}")
   108	
   109	    def edges_from(self, entity_id: str) -> tuple[Relationship, ...]:
   110	        """The edges this entity inherits along, in model order."""
   111	        return tuple(r for r in self.relationships if r.source_entity_id == entity_id)
   112	
   113	    def definitions(self) -> dict[str, str]:
   114	        """Every definition, by the token that refers to it. Copied, never composed."""
   115	        found: dict[str, str] = {}
   116	        for entity in self.entities:
   117	            found[entity.id] = entity.definition
   118	            for attribute in entity.attributes:
   119	                found[f"{entity.id}.{attribute.id}"] = attribute.definition
   120	        for relationship in self.relationships:
   121	            found[relationship.id] = relationship.definition
   122	        return found
   123	
   124	
   125	class ModelError(Exception):
   126	    """A model this system will not build from."""
   127	
   128	
   129	def _named(kind: str, value: str) -> str:
   130	    """Every id here reaches SQL as an identifier and a file name. names.py says which are safe."""
   131	    if unsafe(value):
   132	        raise ModelError(refuse_unsafe(kind, value))
   133	    return value
   134	
   135	
   136	def read_model(path: Path) -> Model:
   137	    document = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())["model"]
   138	    entities = tuple(
   139	        Entity(
   140	            id=_named("entity", str(entity["id"])),
   141	            definition=str(entity["definition"]),
   142	            attributes=tuple(
   143	                Attribute(
   144	                    id=_named("attribute", str(attribute["id"])),
   145	                    type=AttributeType(str(attribute["type"])),
   146	                    definition=str(attribute["definition"]),
   147	                )
   148	                for attribute in entity["attributes"]
   149	            ),
   150	        )
   151	        for entity in document["entities"]
   152	    )
   153	    relationships = tuple(
   154	        Relationship(
   155	            name=_named("relationship", str(declared["name"])),
   156	            source_entity_id=str(declared["source_entity_id"]),
   157	            target_entity_id=str(declared["target_entity_id"]),
   158	            definition=str(declared["definition"]),
   159	        )
   160	        for declared in document.get("relationships", ())
   161	    )
   162	    return Model(path=path, entities=entities, relationships=relationships)

     1	# The only place the data is explained. Everything else -- contracts, questions, the
     2	# generated layer, the pages -- references these definitions and never restates one.
     3	#
     4	# No source name appears here. Not in an id, not in a name, not in a definition. This is the

     6	# word in it would mean the dependency had been moved rather than broken.
     7	model:
     8	  id: ADSS
     9	  name: ADSS
    10	  definition: What the business means by the things it records.
    11	  description: >-
    12	    One model for the whole platform. Entities arrive as the questions that need them arrive,
    13	    and a new attribute, entity or relationship is always a new structure rather than a change
    14	    to one something already depends on.
    15	
    16	  entities:
    17	    - id: ORDER
    18	      name: ORDER
    19	      definition: >-
    20	        A commitment by the business to supply goods, created when it accepts a customer's
    21	        request for them.
    22	      description: >-
    23	        One order is one such commitment. It begins on the day the business accepts it and is
    24	        settled by delivering what was promised, to where it was promised.
    25	      attributes:
    26	        - id: ORDER_NUMBER
    27	          name: ORDER_NUMBER
    28	          definition: The number the business uses when it refers to one particular order.
    29	          description: Unique across all orders, and never reused once issued.
    30	          type: STRING
    31	          effective_timestamp: false
    32	
    33	        - id: PLACED_ON
    34	          name: PLACED_ON
    35	          definition: The day the business accepted the order, and from which the order exists.
    36	          description: >-
    37	            An order is placed once. This is the date every question about when demand
    38	            occurred is measured against.
    39	          type: START_TIMESTAMP
    40	
    41	        - id: DESTINATION_COUNTRY
    42	          name: DESTINATION_COUNTRY

    46	            question about demand by geography means this unless it says otherwise.
    47	          type: STRING
    48	          effective_timestamp: true
    49	
    50	        - id: SHIPPED_ON
    51	          name: SHIPPED_ON
    52	          definition: The day the goods left the business on their way to the destination.
    53	          description: >-
    54	            An order ships once, or not yet. No day at all means the business has not recorded
    55	            the goods as gone -- which is not a promise that they never will be, and is not the

    98	          type: STRING
    99	          effective_timestamp: false

   118	          type: STRING

   123	      definition: >-

   163	          effective_timestamp: true

1	# Architectural blueprint
     2	
     3	This is the overarching document. It states what the system must achieve and the absolute
     4	principles that support it. It names no technology, no tool, no modelling technique and no
     5	process — those live in [conventions.md](conventions.md) and in [adr/](adr/README.md), and each
     6	must justify itself against what is written here.
     7	
     8	That separation is the point. Every tool this system currently uses must be replaceable without
     9	invalidating a single line below.
    10	
    11	## The vision
    12	
    13	An analytical data storage system is built for requirements that do not exist yet, and it is
    14	changed from the inside by its own use: every question it answers expands what its users want to
    15	ask next. It is therefore judged over a life cycle measured in decades, not over the delivery of
    16	any one data product.
    17	
    18	Four qualities, in no priority order, because a design that sacrifices one for another is a
    19	design that has failed:
    20	
    21	| Quality | What it means here |
    22	|---|---|
    23	| **Maintainable** | A change costs about the same in year ten as in year one. |
    24	| **Scalable** | Adding a source or a consumer strengthens the system rather than making the next addition harder. |
    25	| **Adaptable** | A source replacement, a new entity or a new relationship is absorbed without rewriting what already works. |
    26	| **Good time to market** | Not the fastest possible way. Always within acceptable timing. |
    27	
    28	Speed is deliberately last-named and deliberately qualified. A system that answers today's
    29	question fastest and next year's question not at all has optimised the wrong variable.
    30	
    31	## The three layers
    32	
    33	The layers are named for their **purpose**, never for their position or their quality grade.
    34	They are not bronze, silver and gold; they are not staging, core and marts. Ask three people what
    35	belongs in silver and you get four answers — and these names are also the principles, so a name
    36	that does not carry a principle is a name that cannot be enforced.
    37	
    38	| Layer | Data according to… | What it is |
    39	|---|---|---|
    40	| **DAS** | the **System** | what the source sent us, as it sent it |
    41	| **DAB** | the **Business** | what the business means by it, integrated and source-agnostic |
    42	| **DAR** | the **Requirements** | what a particular consumer needs, shaped for them |
    43	
    44	## Flow
    45	
    46	Flow is one-directional and has exactly three rules. They are absolutes.
    47	
    48	| # | Rule | Why it matters |
    49	|---|---|---|
    50	| F1 | **Analytical usage reads only DAR.** | Consumption against DAS or DAB creates dependencies on structures whose whole purpose is to be free to change. The dependency is invisible until something breaks. |
    51	| F2 | **DAR reads only DAB.** | A data product that reaches past the business layer to a source has bypassed the integration that makes numbers agree, and reintroduces the cascade the architecture exists to break. |
    52	| F3 | **DAB reads only DAS.** | A source connection wired into the business layer means the source dependency was moved, not broken. |
    53	
    54	Each movement between layers does exactly **one** job: ingest, integrate, specialise. Code that
    55	ingests and integrates, or integrates and shapes for a report, has collapsed two layers into one
    56	and is not permitted regardless of how convenient it is.
    57	
    58	## Per-layer principles
    59	
    60	### DAS — data according to the system
    61	
    62	| # | Principle | Why it matters |
    63	|---|---|---|
    64	| S1 | **Capture and persist only.** No business logic, no interpretation, no enrichment. | Interpretation here buries a decision in the one layer that is supposed to make none, and disguises the next source change as a business change. |
    65	| S2 | **Non-volatile.** Nothing is updated. Nothing is deleted. Every load is retained. | DAB and DAR must be rebuildable from DAS at any time without going back to the source. That is what makes changing the layers above it safe. |
    66	| S3 | **Forgiving ingestion, strict unpacking.** Accept whatever arrives; enforce structure at the boundary out. | Committing to a schema at ingest turns every upstream change into lost data. Enforcing nothing on the way out turns every upstream change into a silent one. |
    67	| S4 | **Every data point records where it came from and when.** | Without per-row provenance, an answer that looks wrong cannot be traced, and the only remaining move is to distrust the whole system. |
    68	| S5 | **The source keeps its own words.** | A field renamed to a business term is an interpretation, and S1 forbids interpretations here. |
    69	
    70	### DAB — data according to the business
    71	
    72	| # | Principle | Why it matters |
    73	|---|---|---|
    74	| B1 | **Subject oriented.** Organised around business concepts, never around source systems. | The concepts outlive the systems that happen to record them. |
    75	| B2 | **Integrated.** Semantically and structurally source-agnostic. | Adding a second source for a concept must not add a parallel structure, and removing one must not change any structure at all. This is the property that breaks the dependency. |
    76	| B3 | **Time-variant.** Historized: every version retained, none overwritten. | An answer served last quarter must still be reproducible this quarter, or the system cannot be audited. |
    77	| B4 | **Non-volatile.** Never updated, never deleted. | Same reason as B3, stated as a physical constraint rather than an intention. |
    78	| B5 | **Atomic.** The atomic data point is the base of every semantic meaning. No aggregation, no bucketing, no pre-rollup. | An aggregate here is a requirement leaking down a layer, and it is the reason teams start demanding raw data. |
    79	| B6 | **Reusable.** Nothing exists here because one consumer wanted it. | A construct that only makes sense given one requirement belongs in DAR. |
    80	| B7 | **Change is additive.** A new attribute, entity or relationship is a new structure, never a modification of an existing one. | A modification has a regression surface. An addition does not. Repeated over the thousands of changes a platform absorbs, that difference is the whole ball game. |
    81	| B8 | **Meaning is defined exactly once, here.** | Definitions that exist in two places drift, and the drift surfaces as two reports that disagree. |
    82	
    83	### DAR — data according to the requirements
    84	
    85	| # | Principle | Why it matters |
    86	|---|---|---|
    87	| R1 | **Requirement oriented.** Shaped for a specific consumer, optimised for them. | The integration work is already done; this layer's only job is to be usable. |
    88	| R2 | **No cross-dependency.** A data product owns its structures and does not consume another product's. Duplication between products is accepted deliberately. | Each product has its own rate of change. Sharing structure couples those rates and reintroduces the dependency problem at the consumption layer. |
    89	| R3 | **Reuse the definition, never the instance.** | Consistency comes from a shared *meaning* in DAB, not from a shared *table* here. The conformed dimension buys agreement by sharing structure and pays in coupling; with a real integration layer beneath, that price is unnecessary. |
    90	| R4 | **Volatile and generated.** Nothing here is hand-written or hand-edited. | Anything derived from DAB can be thrown away and rebuilt. An edit to generated output is lost on the next generation, and until then the code and the model quietly disagree. |
    91	| R5 | **What was delivered, to whom, and when is recorded.** | An answer someone acted on must be reconstructable, including the definitions that produced it. |
    92	
    93	## What structure cannot do
    94	
    95	Generation guarantees **consistency**, not **correctness**. A poorly chosen model compiles just
    96	as reliably as a good one, and a system that enforces coherent structure over incoherent
    97	definitions produces coherent-looking incoherence — which is more dangerous than visible mess,
    98	because it is trusted.
    99	
   100	Deciding what an entity is, when two records refer to the same instance, and whether two
   101	attributes carry the same meaning remains human judgement. The effort saved on mechanism is meant
   102	to be redirected to meaning, not removed.
   103	
   104	## No exceptions
   105	
   106	This document contains no exceptions and no pre-authorised bypass. That is deliberate: if a
   107	principle is not stated as an absolute, with its reason recorded, there is nothing to break, and
   108	a deviation becomes indistinguishable from an ordinary decision.
   109	
   110	Reality still wins sometimes. When it does, the answer is not to weaken the principle but to
   111	**cost the deviation**: which principle breaks, why the conforming option was unworkable here,
   112	what it costs, and the observable condition under which it is removed. That record lives in
   113	[deviations.md](deviations.md), and every deviation has an ADR behind it.

     2	name: dab
     3	description: Work on the DAB layer — dab/model.yaml, the mappings, and the modelling engine. Use when adding an entity, attribute or relationship, editing anything under dab/, running install/deploy/execute, or debugging engine errors, history that looks wrong, or rows that multiply.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# DAB — data according to the business
     7	
     8	The layer that breaks the dependency between source and consumption. It is also **the only
     9	place the data is explained**: every definition lives here and everything else references it.
    10	
    11	## The shape
    12	
    13	```
    14	dab/model.yaml           entities, attributes, relationships -- and their definitions
    15	dab/uss.yaml             what the generated layer needs: events, measures (see the dar skill)
    16	dab/mappings/*.yaml      one per entity: how it is loaded from das__staged
    17	dab/workflow.yaml        the model plus its mappings
    18	dab/connections.yaml     one profile
    19	bin/linux-amd64/daana-cli  the engine, vendored, pinned by the checksum beside it
    20	```
    21	
    22	## Adding an entity
    23	
    24	1. Add it to `dab/model.yaml` in **business language**. No source word may appear — not in an
    25	   id, a name, a definition or a description. If you are typing the source's word for
    26	   something, stop and ask what the business calls it.
    27	2. Add `dab/mappings/<entity>-mapping.yaml`, then add it to `workflow.yaml`.
    28	3. `uv run adss dab deploy && uv run adss dab execute`.
    29	
    30	Every entity, attribute and relationship needs a `definition` written for a person. A missing
    31	one is a blank row in a glossary somebody notices in a screenshot.
    32	
    33	## The seven mapping rules
    34	
    35	They are in `docs/conventions.md` §1.4 and checked by `tests/test_mapping_rules.py`, because
    36	**the engine checks none of them**. Two are not style:
    37	
    38	- **M3 — `FULL_LOG`, always.** `FULL` against a source with more than one row per key inserts
    39	  a duplicate row on every run, forever, and *every presentation view hides it*. Our staged
    40	  change log is multi-row-per-key by construction, so `FULL` is exactly the wrong default and
    41	  its failure is invisible in both of a question's acceptance queries.
    42	- **M2 — exactly one primary key.** Two entries are read as two *alternate identifiers*, not
    43	  as a composite key, and that mode cannot be undone once loaded. Compose with
    44	  `cast(a AS VARCHAR) || '-' || cast(b AS VARCHAR)` — the separator is not cosmetic, and
    45	  **not `concat`**, which ignores nulls and turns a missing half into a shorter key that collides
    46	  with a real one. `||` yields null and fails at the engine instead. Two entries are refused at
    47	  deploy unless `allow_multiple_identifiers` is set, and with it the key becomes a minted UUID.
    48	  A generated check counts the composed key against the source's own parts on every build, so a
    49	  separator that is wrong for the data that landed fails then rather than merging two rows in
    50	  silence. ADR 0010.
    51	
    52	## Ids
    53	
    54	An id in `model.yaml`, `uss.yaml` or a mapping becomes three things: a quoted SQL identifier, a
    55	string literal inside a generated check, and the stem of a file under `checks/`. A letter, then
    56	letters, digits and underscores — refused at read time otherwise, because a quote in an event id
    57	closes the literal and comments out the rest, so the check runs and reports nothing wrong for
    58	ever, and a slash writes the file outside `checks/`.
    59	
    60	That is not a security boundary and the record does not pretend it is. Whoever can edit these
    61	files can already run arbitrary SQL: the engine compiles a mapping's `transformation_expression`
    62	verbatim into a view over the same warehouse, and sqlfluff is a formatter, not a validator —
    63	injected multi-statement SQL passes through it unchanged.
    64	
    65	## What the engine does and does not do
    66	
    67	The whole type vocabulary is `STRING`, `NUMBER`, `UNIT`, `START_TIMESTAMP`, `END_TIMESTAMP`.
    68	There is no plain date type; a business date is `START_TIMESTAMP`.
    69	
    70	A version is dated by `entity_effective_timestamp_expression`, which is always `extracted_at`
    71	here — so DAB's history is what the system observed and when. That wins even when the entity
    72	has a `START_TIMESTAMP` attribute; confirmed, not assumed.
    73	
    74	## Things that cost a day if you do not know them
    75	
    76	- **`daana framework is not installed on the remote database` means the file is busy.** The
    77	  lock is per process: the engine is a subprocess, and it cannot take the lock while we hold
    78	  it. `require_detached` refuses before that happens; if you see the message anyway, close
    79	  whatever has the warehouse open.
    80	- **`<entity>_focal` and `<entity>_idfr` are created and never populated** on this platform.
    81	  Anything joining to them returns nothing, with no error. DAR reads the `view_*` layer only.
    82	- **`view_<entity>_with_rel` is two different things and its name says neither.** On a
    83	  relationship's **source** side it is a passthrough: its columns are identical to
    84	  `view_<entity>`, and it carries no relationship key at all. On a relationship's **target**
    85	  side it becomes a join back to the source entity and gains that entity's key *and every one
    86	  of its attributes*, one row per source row — so it **fans out**, and summing the target's own
    87	  measure over it multiplies. Measured on a probe: 200.75 against a true 150.75. Never read it.
    88	- **Relationship keys come from `v_<src>_<name>_<tgt>`**, which is the raw pair table plus a
    89	  `rel_name` column. Not `view_<src>_<name>_<tgt>`: that one is a *current* view, ranked with
    90	  `rank()` — so it re-points a child's whole history at whichever target it points at now, and
    91	  returns two rows for a child that named two targets at one instant. ADR 0006.
    92	- **A null foreign key is never retracted.** The engine's reader drops null targets, so
    93	  "belongs to nobody" cannot be expressed: re-landing a row with a null key writes nothing at
    94	  all — no row, no tombstone, no `row_st` flip — and the stale pair survives forever.
    95	- **`type_key` is not stable** across models or even across entities within one. Resolve a
    96	  relationship by name, never by number.
    97	- **Object names keep the model's casing**: `view_ORDER`, not `view_order`. Identifiers
    98	  resolve case-insensitively, so a consumer may write either — but code matching names out of
    99	  the catalog must normalise.
   100	- Numeric attributes are widened to `DECIMAL(28, 8)` whatever the source declared.
   101	- DuckDB is not in the engine's own list of supported platforms. It works; do not expect the
   102	  vendor to keep it working.

1	---
     2	name: dar
     3	description: Work on the DAR layer — the generated Unified Star Schema, dab/uss.yaml, and the SQL under dar/uss. Use when adding an event or a measure, changing the bridge's column contract, debugging a total that is wrong or multiplied, or when generated SQL and the model have drifted.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# DAR — data according to the requirements
     7	
     8	One bridge, one peripheral per entity, one calendar. **Nothing here is hand-written**, and a
     9	wrong name is fixed in the model and regenerated. An edit to generated output is lost on the
    10	next generation, and until then the code and the model quietly disagree.
    11	
    12	## The shape
    13	
    14	```
    15	dab/uss.yaml        the declarations: events, their dates, their measures
    16	dar/uss/*.sql       generated and committed
    17	```
    18	
    19	`uv run adss dar generate` writes them; `--check` fails if the committed SQL is not what the
    20	model produces; `uv run adss dar build` runs them.
    21	
    22	## The column contract
    23	
    24	Everything downstream is written against these names and will not survive them changing. A
    25	model change **appends**; it never rearranges.
    26	
    27	| column | what it is |
    28	|---|---|
    29	| `_stage` | the entity this row is a row *of* |
    30	| `_event` | the event, lower-cased |
    31	| `_event_date` | joins `_calendar.date_key` |
    32	| `_is_current` | always true on a transaction stage |
    33	| `_observed_at` | the DAB effective timestamp, which is the DAS extraction time |
    34	| `<entity>_key` | one per entity, in model order |
    35	| `_measure__<entity>__<measure>` | one per measure; **non-null only on the owning stage** |
    36	
    37	## The one rule that matters most
    38	
    39	**Keys inherit; measures do not.** A stage carries the key of every entity it reaches along
    40	many-to-one relationships, and a measure is non-null only on the stage that owns it. Copying a
    41	parent's measure onto its children multiplies it when summed — that is the fan trap, and
    42	avoiding it is the entire reason there is a bridge rather than one wide join.
    43	
    44	Slice 4 measured it on two grains rather than asserting it: 2,155 line rows carry an order key
    45	and the order's freight stays at 64,942.69. `tests/test_fan_out.py` is that measurement, and a
    46	generated check per measure repeats it on every build.
    47	
    48	**The half that is false.** The bridge protects the measure *column*. It protects nothing on a
    49	peripheral — and a numeric attribute that is also a measure's source is published in **both**
    50	places. `sum(o.freight_charge)` over `_bridge ⨝ order` returns 207,306.10 against a true
    51	64,942.69: once per line. It is one join and one sum, and it looks exactly like an answer.
    52	
    53	Three consequences at query time, none of which the schema can enforce:
    54	
    55	- A join on the row's own `_stage` key may be `INNER`. A join on an **inherited** key must be
    56	  `LEFT`.
    57	- A ratio is `sum(a) / sum(b)` at query time. It is never a stored measure: an average of
    58	  averages is wrong at every grain but the one it was computed at.
    59	- **Aggregate `_measure__` columns and nothing else.** A question's `uss.sql` is refused if it
    60	  applies any aggregate to a peripheral's column, or writes `count(*)` over the bridge — which
    61	  counts measurement events rather than the thing asked about. Checked on the engine's parse
    62	  tree, so a cast, a window or a subquery does not get past it. ADR 0012.
    63	
    64	## Adding a measure
    65	
    66	Add it to `dab/uss.yaml` under its event, with a **definition** — the glossary copies these
    67	verbatim and never composes one. Name it `<descriptor>_<entities>_<unit>`, entity plural, no
    68	scope or aggregation words: `placed_orders_count`, never `total_orders`. Then regenerate.
    69	
    70	## Things worth knowing
    71	
    72	- The generator reads `view_<entity>_hist` and keeps the latest version **in which the event's
    73	  date is set**, so an entity the event never happened to has no row for it by construction
    74	  rather than by a filter someone has to remember.
    75	- It never reads `_focal` or `_idfr` (empty on this platform) or `_with_rel` (a passthrough on
    76	  a relationship's source side, and a fanned-out join on its target side — see the dab skill).
    77	- **An inherited key comes from `v_<src>_<name>_<tgt>`, ranked here rather than by the engine**,
    78	  as of the observation time of the row that inherits it, `row_st = 'Y'` only, matched on
    79	  `rel_name`, joined LEFT, and ranked with `row_number()` and an explicit tiebreak so it cannot
    80	  fan out. Every clause of that sentence is load-bearing; ADR 0006 says which failure each one
    81	  prevents.
    82	- **It never invents a member.** A null dimension stays null. A question that wants nulls
    83	  grouped or excluded says so in its own file, because that is a property of the question.
    84	- Layout is the linter's, applied *inside* the generator. Do not hand-format emitted SQL and
    85	  do not run a formatter over `dar/uss` afterwards — either produces a diff on every
    86	  regeneration.
    87	- A zero-edge walk is a valid walk. One entity and no relationships is the normal case.
    88	- **An event may be dated by a date it inherits**: `date_attribute: ORDER.PLACED_ON` on an event
    89	  whose entity reaches `ORDER`. The date is resolved in the same CTE and at the same instant as
    90	  the key, off the same parent row, so the two cannot disagree. A row whose inherited date does
    91	  not resolve gets **no bridge row** — filtered where it was resolved, because the version CTE
    92	  has no such column to filter. Without that the row would arrive dated null and the calendar's
    93	  inner join would drop it, which looks exactly like the rule working. A generated check compares
    94	  the inherited date against the stage that *owns* it, which is independent because the two come
    95	  through different CTEs; it is generated only where such a stage exists, since a check that
    96	  re-derives what it expects from the generator agrees with a broken generator. ADR 0009.
    97	- **A composed key is measured, not argued about.** Where a source key is composite the mapping
    98	  joins the parts with a separator, and a generated check counts the composition against the
    99	  parts on every build. A separator that is wrong for the data that landed says so then. ADR
   100	  0010.
